home.title: Internet Monitor — Document outages, complain with proof
home.description: Free app for Windows, Mac and Linux that records every internet outage and slowdown and turns it into proof for your provider. No account, no tracking.
home.eyebrow: Free · Windows, Mac, Linux · No account
home.hero_title: Document your outages. Complain with proof.
home.hero_sub: Internet Monitor quietly watches your home internet. Every time it drops or slows down, it writes down when, for how long, and why. When you call your provider, you have the facts, not just a feeling.
home.hero_alt: The Internet Monitor dashboard: connection status, delay, outage timeline and tips about your line
home.benefits_sub: Calling your provider without proof rarely works. This app gives you the proof.

benefits.title: Every outage, written down
benefits.body: The exact start time, how long it lasted, and which part failed. Even the short drops you didn't notice.

benefits.title: Your router or your provider?
benefits.body: It tells you whether the problem is in your home or at your provider, so you know who to call.

benefits.title: A complaint, ready to send
benefits.body: One click gives you a complaint text built from your own measurements, plus an evidence file to attach.

benefits.title: Is your speed what you pay for?
benefits.body: Run speed tests, or schedule them, and compare the results with the speed in your contract.

home.shots_sub: Simple screens that show what your internet really did.

shots.overview: Live status, the last 24 hours, and plain tips about your line
shots.complaints: Your complaints, the provider's deadline, and the proof for each one
shots.report: A monthly report you can save as PDF and send
shots.history: Every outage of the day, with its time, length and cause

home.promise_sub: Your internet history is yours. It never leaves your computer unless you send it.
promise: No account and nothing to sign up for
No ads, no tracking, no analytics
Your data stays on your computer
Free for home and work, with the code in the open
home.final_sub: Install it once, leave it running, and let the facts build up.

download.title: Download Internet Monitor — Windows, Mac, Linux, Pi
download.description: Download Internet Monitor for free and install it in a few minutes, with simple steps for Windows, Mac, Linux and Raspberry Pi.
download.intro: Free, no account needed. We pick the right file for your computer. Press the big button and follow the short steps.
download.detected: You're on {os}. This button is the one for you.
download.detected_pi: This looks like a Raspberry Pi. Look at the Advanced section at the bottom of the page.
download.phone: Internet Monitor runs on a computer. Open this page on your computer to download it. You can then check the dashboard from your phone.

os_sub.mac: Apple chip (M1 and newer) or Intel
os_sub.pi: Runs 24/7, you open it from your phone or PC

download.tray_desc: A small icon sits next to the clock. Click it to open the dashboard whenever you like. This is the best choice for most people.
download.window_desc: It opens in its own window. On Windows you can shrink it next to the clock. On Mac and Linux, closing the window stops it.
download.pick_first: Not sure? Choose the first one.
download.mac_arm_sub: M1, M2, M3, M4 and newer
download.mac_which: Not sure which Mac you have? Click the Apple menu, then **About This Mac**. If it says **Chip: Apple**, pick Apple chip. If it says **Processor: Intel**, pick Intel.
download.mac_show_both: Not the right one? Show both
download.preview_only: Only in the preview for now
download.fallback: We couldn't load the list of files right now. All the files are on the downloads page on GitHub.
download.preview_body: Version {version} ({date}) is a test version with the newest features. It may still have bugs. The app never switches to a preview on its own.
download.install_sub: A few quick steps, only the first time.

windows: Download the file with the big button above.
Look for a small icon next to the clock. Click the **^** arrow if you can't see it.
Click the icon and choose **Open dashboard**.
mac: Download the file made for your Mac.
Allow it to run, one time only.
Right-click the file, choose **Open**, then **Open** again.
Click the small icon at the top of the screen and choose **Open dashboard**.
linux: Allow it to run, one time only.
Double-click the file to start it.
Click the small icon and choose **Open dashboard**. In the regular program edition, the window opens by itself.
pi: Download the file for your device above.
In a terminal, run **chmod +x** on the file, then start it with **--listen 0.0.0.0** so your phone and PC can reach it.
It prints a link with your private key. Open it from any phone or computer at home.
To start it automatically after a power cut, follow the full guide.

warn.windows: Windows may show a blue box saying **Windows protected your PC**. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. It shows up because the app is new, not because anything is wrong.
warn.mac: If your Mac says it can't be opened because the developer is unknown, go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll down and click **Open Anyway**.

more.mac: Open the **Terminal** app (find it with Spotlight). Type **chmod +x** and a space, drag the downloaded file into the window, then press Enter.
more.linux: Right-click the file, choose **Properties → Permissions**, and tick **Allow executing file as program**. Or run **chmod +x** on it in a terminal.

download.folder_tip: Tip: keep the file in its own folder, for example **Internet Monitor** inside Documents. The app saves its records next to the file.
download.other_sub: Pick another system to see its download button.
download.advanced_sub: For Raspberry Pi, home servers and people who like to check the details.
download.pi_note: These versions have no window. You open the dashboard from another device on your network.
download.advanced_sums: Check your download with the SHA256SUMS file
download.advanced_all: All versions and release notes on GitHub
download.advanced_source: Build it yourself from the source code

guide.title: Beginner's guide — your first complaint in 6 steps
guide.description: A simple guide to Internet Monitor: install it, leave it running, and send your provider a complaint backed by real measurements.
guide.intro: No tech skills needed. Follow the pictures, from "my internet keeps dropping" to a complaint your provider can't ignore.

steps.title: Download and open it
steps.body: Press the big button on the download page, then double-click the file.
steps.alt: A downloaded Internet Monitor file, ready to open

steps.title: Find the small icon
steps.body: Look next to the clock, click the icon and choose **Open dashboard**.
steps.alt: The bar next to the clock with the Internet Monitor icon and its menu showing Open dashboard

steps.title: Leave it running
steps.body: Keep your computer on. The app checks your internet all day and writes down every drop.
steps.alt: The home screen saying Connected, highlighted

steps.title: Add your line details
steps.body: Open **Complaints** and fill in your company and plan. They stay on your computer.
steps.alt: The Your internet line form on the Complaints page, highlighted

steps.title: When the internet drops, open Complaints
steps.body: It lists every drop from the last 7 days.
steps.alt: The Complaints menu item and the card with your last 7 days, next to the Log a complaint button

steps.title: Copy the text and the proof
steps.body: Press **Copy text** and **Download evidence (ZIP)**, then send both to your provider.
steps.alt: The Copy text and Download evidence (ZIP) buttons, highlighted

tips: The monthly report (History → Monthly report → Print or save as PDF) covers the whole month in one page.
Alerts can reach your phone through Telegram, Discord or ntfy when the internet drops.
guide.advanced_note: Want it to run all day on a Raspberry Pi? See the Advanced section on the download page.
